lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Skill model: what a job actually involves day to day

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic what a job actually involves day to day task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner selects one job title from their earlier inventory, writes their honest prior assumption about a typical day, then researches using two different sources (such as a career-information resource and a written or video first-person account) and records what a typical day actually involves.
safetyNotes: If the learner cannot access two independent sources, the reference profile provided with this lesson counts as one full source on its own.
materials: learner-local: a job title from the learner's interest inventory

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Does the real day-to-day make you more or less interested in this job, and what specific task caused that reaction?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g10-u01-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Source use: Two sources (or the reference profile as one full source) are used and summarized. | Task-level specificity: Summary names at least three concrete tasks from the research. | Prediction-versus-reality comparison: Names one accurate and one inaccurate part of the prediction, citing the sources. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner research the same job at a different level of experience (entry-level versus several years in) and describe how the day-to-day changes with experience.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic what a job actually involves day to day task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: what a job actually involves day to day worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner selects one job title from their earlier inventory, writes their honest prior assumption about a typical day, then researches using two different sources (such as a career-information resource and a written or video first-person account) and records what a typical day actually involves.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact what a job actually involves day to day decision or action.
Model move 2: Before researching, write your honest prediction of what a typical day looks like in this job.
Model move 3: Using two sources (or the provided reference profile as one full source), record what a typical day actually involves.

Model check: Source use: Two sources (or the reference profile as one full source) are used and summarized. | Task-level specificity: Summary names at least three concrete tasks from the research. | Prediction-versus-reality comparison: Names one accurate and one inaccurate part of the prediction, citing the sources.

resources.title: what a job actually involves day to day action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for what a job actually involves day to day.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: what a job actually involves day to day coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner selects one job title from their earlier inventory, writes their honest prior assumption about a typical day, then researches using two different sources (such as a career-information resource and a written or video first-person account) and records what a typical day actually involves.
Coach direction: Before researching, write your honest prediction of what a typical day looks like in this job.
Learner prompt: Describe what you currently assume a typical day in this job looks like, hour by hour if you can.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: what a job actually involves day to day complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Using two sources (or the provided reference profile as one full source), record what a typical day actually involves.
Response 1 (t2-p1): Summarize what your first source says a typical day involves, including one task you did not expect.
Response 2 (t2-p2): Summarize what your second source says, and note any point where the two sources disagree or emphasize different things.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I used two distinct sources, or the provided reference profile counted as one full source.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: what a job actually involves day to day minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Does the real day-to-day make you more or less interested in this job, and what specific task caused that reaction?

Success checks: Source use: Two sources (or the reference profile as one full source) are used and summarized. | Task-level specificity: Summary names at least three concrete tasks from the research. | Prediction-versus-reality comparison: Names one accurate and one inaccurate part of the prediction, citing the sources.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: what a job actually involves day to day supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g10-u01-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional what a job actually involves day to day condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Source use: Two sources (or the reference profile as one full source) are used and summarized. | Task-level specificity: Summary names at least three concrete tasks from the research. | Prediction-versus-reality comparison: Names one accurate and one inaccurate part of the prediction, citing the sources..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u01-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
